**The meaning of the verse**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾
O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: avoid much evil suspicion of the believers; some of that suspicion is a sin. Do not search out the private faults of the Muslims, and let none of you say behind another's back what he would dislike. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when he is dead? You would hate that, so hate backbiting him. And fear Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. Allah accepts the repentance of His believing servants and is Merciful to them.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Hassan saw his neighbour going out at night. When did his mistake begin: when the questions came into his mind, or when he climbed onto the roof to wait and then walked after him? (A passing thought comes and goes and there is no sin in it; the sin is in following people and searching into their affairs.)
2. Hassan told himself, "If there's something bad going on, I'll be the first to protect the alley from it." Does this excuse make spying allowed? (No. Whoever sees an obvious danger tells their family or someone able to deal with it, and does not follow people or search out their secrets.)
3. What was Uncle Marzouq's secret? And why could Hassan not look him in the eye in the morning?

**This week's exercise**
"A closed door": this week your child knocks and asks permission before going into any closed room, and does not open anyone's bag, phone or notebook without permission. And be their example: ask their permission before you open their things.
